Investigated the genuinely validate-specific obligation ('Validate each layer independently, aggregate stable diagnostics, distinguish errors from interoperability warnings, and never repair or normalize unless explicitly requested') against lifecycle.py's validate() and _layer_png_diagnostics, plus test_obligation_lifecycle_and_write.py. Confirmed independent per-layer validation (test_multi_layer_validation_checks_all_sources: a two-layer document with one bad source reports exactly one diagnostic, naming only the bad layer) and stable diagnostic aggregation (structured report, not exceptions) are both directly proven.

3. Checked 'never repair or normalize unless explicitly requested' against validate()'s actual signature: no auto-fix parameter exists, and the function returns a report without mutating input. The only recovery path in the package at all is ReadMode.TOLERANT on load() -- a separate, explicitly opt-in code path, not something validate() itself does. Confirmed proven, not assumed.

4. Checked 'distinguish errors from interoperability warnings' by grepping lifecycle.py for Severity.WARNING usage: zero hits. Every Diagnostic this package constructs uses Severity.ERROR, even though the shared Diagnostic/Severity type (from format_factory.core) already supports WARNING. Confirmed this is a real, standing gap -- not an audit backlog item -- and corrected the obligation to accurate partial with a precise missing_behavior naming exactly this, rather than force-promoting the whole obligation on the strength of the three proven clauses.
